items.exemplar:
A. Congress created the Freedmen's Bureau (1865) to provide food, schools, and labor contracts for formerly enslaved people — the first large-scale federal welfare agency.

B. The Fourteenth Amendment (1868) made freedpeople citizens and guaranteed them 'equal protection of the laws,' giving the federal government a constitutional weapon against Southern discrimination.

C. White Southerners resisted through Black Codes (1865–66) that restricted Black movement and labor, and through terror groups like the Ku Klux Klan that murdered Black and white Republicans.
parts: A. Briefly explain ONE way the federal government tried to assist African Americans during Reconstruction.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND such federal effort.
C. Briefly explain ONE way white Southerners resisted those federal efforts.
items.stimulus:
"All persons born or naturalized in the United States... are citizens of the United States... No State shall make or enforce any law which shall abridge the privileges or immunities of citizens... nor deny to any person within its jurisdiction the equal protection of the laws."
—Fourteenth Amendment, Section 1, ratified 1868
